extra.message: The HTML template (HTML_PREFIX) sent with every response contains JavaScript that reads the URL fragment (document.location.hash 'lang=' parameter), decodes it with decodeURIComponent, and writes it into the DOM via document.write without any sanitization. extra.message: The request handler do_GET implements critical operations (arbitrary file read, URL fetching, OS command execution, Python code execution via exec, full database access) with no authentication or authorization checks anywhere. extra.message: The user-controlled query parameter params['id'] (parsed from the request query string at line 26) is concatenated directly into the SQL statement executed by cursor.execute() with no parameterization or escaping. Injected values are additionally rendered unescaped into the HTML table at line 31, enabling XSS through UNION-based injection.

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: The 'v' query parameter is interpolated into the re.sub() replacement string that is injected into the HTML page without any HTML escaping, so arbitrary markup and JavaScript are reflected back to the user, e.g. /?v=<script>alert(1)</script>.

extra.message: The user-supplied 'object' query parameter is passed directly to pickle.loads(). cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: The 'path' query parameter is passed to open(os.path.abspath(params['path'])) with no validation, allowlist, or root confinement, allowing arbitrary local file reads via path traversal (e.g. /?path=../../../../etc/passwd) and full source code disclosure (/?path=dsvw.py).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: When the 'path' parameter contains '://', its value is passed to urllib.request.urlopen() without any URL scheme or host validation, so the server can be used as a proxy to fetch arbitrary targets: internal network services (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:631), file:// URLs for local file reads, and link-local cloud metadata endpoints — a server-side request forgery vulnerability.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: The 'domain' query parameter is concatenated into the shell command string ('nslookup ' + params['domain']) which is executed via subprocess.run(..., shell=True). Appending shell metacharacters yields arbitrary OS command injection, e.g. /?domain=www.google.com; ifconfig.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: User-controlled XML from the 'xml' parameter is parsed with lxml.etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False), which loads DTDs, resolves external entities, and permits network access. An attacker can declare an entity referencing file:///etc/passwd (local file disclosure returned in the response body) or a remote http:// URL (outbound request / blind SSRF).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The 'name' query parameter is formatted directly into an XPath expression (".//user[name/text()='%s']") without escaping. A single quote terminates the string literal and lets an attacker alter the query to extract arbitrary values from the users XML document, e.g. /?name=admin' and substring(password/text(),3,1)='n to blind-extract the admin password.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: The 'size' query parameter controls both the length of each generated string ('#' * int(params['size'])) and the number of iterations (range(int(params['size']))) with no upper bound. A single request such as /?size=9999999 allocates roughly size-squared characters in memory, enabling trivial remote denial of service through uncontrolled resource consumption.

extra.message: The comment-creation operation (lines 48-51) is a state-changing request with no CSRF token, no SameSite cookie attribute, and no Origin/Referer validation, and is invocable via a plain GET request. extra.message: Login credentials are concatenated directly into the SQL query. Although the username is filtered to word characters, the password is inserted into the WHERE clause with no sanitization or parameterization, so a quote in the password breaks the string literal and enables SQL injection with full authentication bypass, e.g. /login?username=admin&password=' OR '1' LIKE '1.

extra.message: The login handler is implemented only in do_GET and reads the password from the URL query string, so credentials are transmitted in URLs and will be recorded in server logs, browser history, bookmarks, and Referer headers.

extra.message: The session cookie is set (via a <meta http-equiv="Set-Cookie"> tag) as 'SESSIONID=<token>; path=/' without the Secure flag or the HttpOnly flag, exposing the session token to interception over unencrypted connections and to theft through JavaScript (document.cookie).

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The SESSIONID token is generated with random.sample(), which is backed by the non-cryptographic Mersenne Twister PRNG, instead of a cryptographically secure generator such as secrets. Session identifiers produced this way are predictable to an attacker who can observe outputs.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: On any exception the full output of traceback.format_exc() — including absolute filesystem paths, source code lines, SQL statements, and internal state — is returned to the client as the response body, disclosing sensitive internal information (full path disclosure) that aids further attacks.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Responses are sent (lines 75-79) without any anti-framing protection — no X-Frame-Options header and no Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive — so application pages can be embedded in attacker-controlled iframes and used for clickjacking/UI-redressing attacks.

cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure

extra.message: The server explicitly sends the header 'X-XSS-Protection: 0' on every response, deliberately disabling the browser's built-in reflected-XSS auditor. This security misconfiguration removes a defense-in-depth layer and makes the reflected, stored, and DOM-based XSS vulnerabilities more reliably exploitable.

cwe: CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: The 'charset' query parameter is interpolated into the Content-Type response header value without validation. Because the value is URL-decoded (line 26) and http.server's send_header() performs no CRLF checks, an attacker can inject %0D%0A sequences to split the HTTP response and inject arbitrary headers and response-body content (HTTP response/header injection, usable for phishing and cache poisoning).

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Response Splitting')
